title: em.json 1.1 — the Extended Matrix container
description: An em.json document is a CONTAINER: a header and one or more graphs, each with its nodes, edges and, optionally, its layout. Special members (the shelf, the DTC corpus, the periodizations) are graphs marked by data.em_collection. Readers MUST ignore keys they do not know; writers of the official tools never write keys prefixed 'x-', which are reserved to third-party extensions. The flat single-graph form of 1.0 ({header, graph}) is described by em.v1.schema.json and is still read by every conforming reader. Specification: https://w3id.org/extendedmatrix/spec/em-json/ — editor Emanuel Demetrescu (CNR-ISPC). This schema is dedicated to the public domain (CC0 1.0).

graphs.description: The members of the container, keyed by member id. A study graph's member id is its graph_id; the special members use conventional ids (shelf, dtc, periodizations) but are recognised by data.em_collection, never by the id.

active_graph_id.description: The study graph that was in front when the file was saved. A reader that finds no such member falls back to the first study graph.

layout.description: A COPY of the active graph's layout, for readers that know only one layout per file (files before 2 Oct 2026, Heriverse). The member's own layout wins.

text.description: A text. Writers omit an empty value; readers treat null as absent.

version.description: The version of the FORM (semver): a reader refuses a MAJOR it does not know and reads every minor of its major. 1.0 = the flat form and the container written before this specification; 1.1 = the container as specified here.

schema_version.description: The version of the CONTENT within the form, an integer that grows when a migration may need to key off it (absent = 0, a file older than the field). Never a reason to refuse a file.

last_editor.description: The application that last saved the file, when it is not the generator (e.g. 'EMStudio 1.6.0-dev.58').

datamodel_versions.description: The versions of the EM datamodels the content follows: nodes, connections, qualia.

ontology_versions.description: The versions of the ontologies the datamodels map to (CIDOC-CRM, CRMarchaeo, CRMem…).

visibility.description: Who may read the study without a token: public, restricted (the default when absent), private.

kind.description: What the study is about: site (the default) or landscape.

composition.description: A landscape cites the studies it is made of: references, never copies. Each item is a string or {id, code, title}. 'part_studies' is an older name, read only.

owner.description: The account that owns the study on a StratiGraph node (written by the server).

embargo.description: An embargo set on a StratiGraph node: a date (ISO 8601) or an object the server defines. Licence and embargo of the CONTENT are nodes of the graph, not header keys.

room.description: Where the study is shared: {node, room_id} (written by EM Tools).

graph_id.description: The graph's id; when absent the member id is used.

code.description: The study's code (GT16), a mirror of StudyNode.data.code written at every save; the study node wins on read.

code_proposed.description: Present (true) while the code is a proposal nobody confirmed.

data.description: Graph-level data. data.em_collection marks a special member.

em_collection.description: ShelfGraph (the project shelf: authors, licences, shared documents), DTCCorpus (the documentation: acquisitions, transformations, the resources they are about), Periodizations (the shared measures of time: periodizations and their horizons). A reader that does not know a value treats the member as an ordinary graph.

active_periodization.description: In the Periodizations member: the id of the periodization in use.

links.description: Relations from a node of this graph to a node of ANOTHER graph of the same container (the address graph → node). A broken link is reported, never a reason to refuse the file.

id.description: Stable identifier (a UUID for nodes born in the official tools).

node_type.description: The type, as named by the EM node datamodel (US, USVs, EpochNode, property, document, geo_position, periodization, horizon…). A reader that does not know a type keeps the node as a generic one.

data.description: The node's fields, as declared by the node datamodel for its type.

edge_type.description: The relation, as named by the EM connections datamodel (is_after, has_same_time, abuts, has_property, extracted_from…).

source.description: The id of a node of the same graph.

target.description: The id of a node of the same graph.

edge_attributes.description: Optional facts about the edge itself (since schema_version 1).

origin.description: On a relative-chronology edge (is_after, has_same_time, changed_from): computed from the physical relations, written by a person, or read from another software's file.

derived.description: The edge was computed by a propagation, not drawn.

derived_from.description: What a derived edge stands for: the id of the edge it was propagated from, or the ids of the physical relations it was derived from.

created_by.description: Editorial stamp: who drew the edge (as on nodes, in data).

removed.description: Tombstone of a removed edge (collaborative editing): the edge stays in the file, marked, so that a merge does not bring it back.

source.description: The id of a node of THIS graph.

layout.description: How a graph is drawn. Optional and reconstructable: a reader may lay the graph out afresh.

swimlanes.description: The rows of the matrix, one per epoch.

group_spaces.description: Group id → the positions inside the group's own space.

edge_routes.description: Edge id → the bends of its line, [x, y] points.

pinned.description: Node ids that keep their exact box through a re-layout.

anchors.description: A node drawn next to another one (a date beside its unit): the corner of 'to' it sits at and the offset.

sketches.description: Shapes placed in the 3D space and not yet proxies of a unit (EMStudio): the person's work, saved with the view.

project_version.description: Which revision of the WORK this file is (not of the format).

id.description: Content digest of this version, 'sha256:<12 hex>'.
